# SugarMount

> SugarMount is the developer name used by simpest, an independent developer, to publish apps on Google Play. Ten SugarMount apps are on Google Play, from a Korean spelling checker and an HWP viewer to photo tools and two puzzle games.

Contact: sugarmount21@gmail.com. Korean pages live at https://sugarmount21.com/, English pages at https://sugarmount21.com/en/.

- [All apps](https://sugarmount21.com/en/apps/) · [앱 전체 (Korean)](https://sugarmount21.com/apps/)
- [About SugarMount](https://sugarmount21.com/en/about/) · [소개 (Korean)](https://sugarmount21.com/about/)
- [RSS feed (English)](https://sugarmount21.com/en/rss.xml) · [RSS 피드 (Korean)](https://sugarmount21.com/rss.xml)
- [Site map: every page](https://sugarmount21.com/en/sitemap/) · [사이트맵 (Korean)](https://sugarmount21.com/sitemap/) · [XML sitemap](https://sugarmount21.com/sitemap.xml)

## Apps

- [SugarSpeller / 한글 띄어쓰기](https://sugarmount21.com/en/apps/sugarspeller/): Fixes Korean spelling and spacing in one pass, from pasted or shared text. Package com.sugarmount.sugarspeller, on Google Play.
- [SugarCard / 생생카드](https://sugarmount21.com/en/apps/sugarcard/): Make Lunar New Year, Chuseok and Christmas greeting cards and send them right away. Package com.sugarmount.sugarcard, on Google Play.
- [SugarAlbum / 슈가앨범](https://sugarmount21.com/en/apps/sugaralbum/): Pick photos, get a video. Package com.sugarmount.sugaralbum, on Google Play.
- [SugarClip](https://sugarmount21.com/en/apps/sugarclip/): Copy text and it goes to your note app, and into your clip history. Package com.sugarmount.sugarclip, on Google Play.
- [Compress Image / 사진 용량 줄이기](https://sugarmount21.com/en/apps/image-compress/): Shrinks photos under a size limit, like 100 KB or 500 KB. Package com.sugarmount.sugarcompress, on Google Play.
- [Flip & Rotate Image / 사진 반전·회전](https://sugarmount21.com/en/apps/image-flip/): Flip and rotate photos, saved as new files. Package com.sugarmount.sugarflip, on Google Play.
- [Convert Image JPG PNG WEBP / 이미지 변환 JPG·PNG·WebP](https://sugarmount21.com/en/apps/image-convert/): HEIC, PNG and WebP to JPG and more, in batches. Package com.sugarmount.sugarconvert, on Google Play.
- [HWP Viewer SugarDoc / 한글뷰어 슈가독](https://sugarmount21.com/en/apps/doc-viewer/): Open Korean HWP/HWPX documents and PDFs you receive, and find them again. Package com.sugarmount.sugardoc, on Google Play.
- [Arrow Knots / 화살표 매듭풀기](https://sugarmount21.com/en/apps/arrow-knots/): Slide tangled arrows out one by one and clear the board. Package com.sugarmount.arrows, on Google Play.
- [Block Turn / 한판블록](https://sugarmount21.com/en/apps/blocks/): A block puzzle: turn a stuck board around with three set pieces. Package com.sugarmount.blocks, on Google Play.
- [AXFamily](https://sugarmount21.com/en/apps/axfamily/): Share family plans and things to bring in one place. Package com.sugarmount.axfamily, coming soon.
- [CarDrawer / 차서랍](https://sugarmount21.com/en/apps/cardrawer/): One drawer per car. AI files every receipt and flags what's missing. Package com.sugarmount.cardrawer, coming soon.
- [TrimBox / 트림박스](https://sugarmount21.com/en/apps/trimbox/): Will your camping gear fit the trunk? Fit it first. Then go. Package com.sugarmount.trimbox, coming soon.

## Facts

- Who makes SugarMount apps? SugarMount is the developer name used by simpest, an independent developer, to publish apps on Google Play. Planning, development and support are all done by the same person.
- Are my photos or documents uploaded? Compress Image, Flip & Rotate Image, Convert Image, HWP Viewer SugarDoc and SugarAlbum process files on your device without uploading them. SugarSpeller sends the text you check to the Naver or Daum spelling checker. Each app's privacy policy has the details.
- Are the apps free? All apps are free to install. Some show ads and offer ad removal or Pro features as a one-time purchase or subscription. HWP Viewer SugarDoc has no ads.
- How do I get support or report a bug? Email sugarmount21@gmail.com. Including the app name, device model and Android version helps us check faster.

## Help articles (English)

- [We're looking for 5 pilot dealerships](https://sugarmount21.com/en/apps/cardrawer/pilot/): CarDrawer is recruiting 5 pilot dealerships: used-car shops of 2 to 10 people in Korea that buy and resell their own stock. 4 weeks free, then the standard rate with a 12-month founding-customer price lock and setup help.
- [Pricing](https://sugarmount21.com/en/apps/cardrawer/pricing/): CarDrawer pricing: Solo ₩59,000, Team ₩149,000, Dealership ₩299,000 per month excluding VAT. 14-day free trial with no card and no automatic billing. No overage charges without consent.
- [Convert an HWP file to PDF on Android](https://sugarmount21.com/en/apps/doc-viewer/hwp-to-pdf/): Open the HWP or HWPX file in SugarDoc, tap ⋮ and Save as PDF to make a PDF on your phone with no upload. Only the first 15 pages are saved.
- [HWP vs HWPX: what differs and how to open both](https://sugarmount21.com/en/apps/doc-viewer/hwp-vs-hwpx/): HWP is the older binary Korean word-processor format; HWPX packs XML files into a ZIP. Renaming one does not convert it. On Android, open both in one viewer.
- [How to open an HWPX or HWP file on Android](https://sugarmount21.com/en/apps/doc-viewer/hwpx-open/): Android phones have no built-in app for Korean HWP and HWPX files. Install a viewer, pick it from Open with, and fix it when it is missing or another app opens.
- [Resize an ID photo for Korean application uploads](https://sugarmount21.com/en/apps/image-compress/id-photo-size/): Set a limit such as 500 KB in Compress Image and your ID photo is saved as a JPEG under it. It does not crop, so crop first when a site fixes pixel sizes.
- [Compress a photo to under 100 KB on Android](https://sugarmount21.com/en/apps/image-compress/photo-under-100kb/): Galaxy Gallery's Resize works by percentage, not file size. Compress Image fits each photo under a KB limit you set, like 100 KB, and flags any it can't fit.
- [Convert HEIC to JPG on a Samsung Galaxy phone](https://sugarmount21.com/en/apps/image-convert/heic-to-jpg/): Old HEIC photos need a converter app or a PC to become JPG. Convert Image does batches on the phone with no upload; HEIC the phone can't decode fails alone.
- [PNG to JPG on Android with a white background](https://sugarmount21.com/en/apps/image-convert/png-to-jpg/): Turning a PNG into a JPG on Android always fills transparent areas with one solid colour. How to pick white and convert several files on the device.
- [Unmirror a selfie on a Samsung Galaxy phone](https://sugarmount21.com/en/apps/image-flip/unmirror-selfie/): Flip a selfie you already took left to right and save it as a new photo: Google Photos for one picture, Flip & Rotate Image for a whole batch.
- [Korean Christmas greeting card messages](https://sugarmount21.com/en/apps/sugarcard/christmas-greetings/): Korean Christmas messages for family, friends and colleagues with English meanings, and how to send one on a card as an image or a 9-second snowfall video.
- [Spell-check long Korean text on Android](https://sugarmount21.com/en/apps/sugarspeller/long-text-check/): Korean web spell checkers take 300 or 1,000 characters at a time. SugarSpeller checks up to 3,000 for free and up to 7,000 with a subscription on Android.

## Help articles (Korean)

- [파일럿 상사 5곳을 모십니다](https://sugarmount21.com/apps/cardrawer/pilot/): 차서랍(CarDrawer) 파일럿 상사 5곳 모집. 직접 매입·재판매하는 2~10인 중고차 매매상사 대상, 4주 무료 후 정상가, 창립 고객 12개월 가격 고정과 설정 대행.
- [요금](https://sugarmount21.com/apps/cardrawer/pricing/): 차서랍(CarDrawer) 요금: 개인 59,000원, 팀 149,000원, 상사 299,000원(월, 부가세 별도). 14일 무료 체험은 카드 없이, 자동 결제 없음. 초과 사용분은 동의 없이 청구하지 않습니다.
- [핸드폰에서 HWP 한글 파일을 PDF로 저장하는 법](https://sugarmount21.com/apps/doc-viewer/hwp-to-pdf/): 한글뷰어 슈가독의 ⋮ 메뉴 'PDF로 저장'을 쓰면 HWP·HWPX 문서를 업로드 없이 휴대폰에서 PDF로 만들 수 있어요. 긴 문서는 처음 15쪽까지 저장되고, 배포용 문서는 저장할 수 없어요.
- [HWP와 HWPX 차이, 휴대폰에서 둘 다 여는 법](https://sugarmount21.com/apps/doc-viewer/hwp-vs-hwpx/): HWP는 한글의 바이너리 형식이고 HWPX는 XML을 ZIP으로 묶은 개방형 형식이에요. 확장자만 바꿔서는 서로 바뀌지 않으니, 휴대폰에서는 두 형식을 모두 여는 뷰어로 보면 돼요.
- [카톡·휴대폰에서 HWPX 파일이 안 열릴 때](https://sugarmount21.com/apps/doc-viewer/hwpx-open/): 휴대폰에는 보통 HWPX·HWP 파일을 여는 앱이 없어요. 한글 뷰어를 설치해 카톡의 '다른 앱으로 열기'에서 고르고, 목록에 없거나 다른 앱이 먼저 열리면 설정을 확인하세요.
- [갤럭시에서 증명사진 용량 줄이는 법](https://sugarmount21.com/apps/image-compress/id-photo-size/): 사진 용량 줄이기 앱에서 상한을 500KB처럼 정하면 증명사진을 그 아래 JPEG로 줄일 수 있어요. 비율에 맞춰 자르지는 않으니 여권처럼 픽셀 규격이 있으면 먼저 잘라야 해요.
- [갤럭시에서 사진을 100KB 이하로 줄이는 법](https://sugarmount21.com/apps/image-compress/photo-under-100kb/): 갤러리 '크기 변경'은 해상도만 바꿔서 몇 KB가 될지 정할 수 없어요. '사진 용량 줄이기' 앱은 100KB·500KB처럼 정한 상한 아래로 사진을 줄이고, 못 맞추면 실패로 알려 줘요.
- [갤럭시에서 HEIC 사진을 JPG로 바꾸는 법](https://sugarmount21.com/apps/image-convert/heic-to-jpg/): 이미 찍은 HEIC 사진은 변환 앱이나 PC로 JPG 새 파일을 만들어야 해요. 이미지 변환 앱은 여러 장을 업로드 없이 휴대폰 안에서 바꾸지만, 기기가 읽지 못하는 HEIC는 그 장만 실패해요.
- [갤럭시에서 PNG를 JPG로 바꾸는 법, 투명 배경은?](https://sugarmount21.com/apps/image-convert/png-to-jpg/): 갤럭시에서 PNG를 JPG로 바꾸면 투명한 부분이 한 가지 색으로 채워져요. 배경을 흰색으로 정해 업로드 없이 여러 장을 바꾸는 순서와 한계를 정리했어요.
- [갤럭시 셀카 좌우반전, 이미 찍은 사진 되돌리는 법](https://sugarmount21.com/apps/image-flip/unmirror-selfie/): 이미 찍은 셀카는 좌우 반전해 새 사진으로 저장하면 돼요. 한 장은 Google 포토의 좌우 반전으로, 여러 장은 사진 반전·회전 앱으로 원본을 그대로 둔 채 한 번에 바꿀 수 있어요.
- [크리스마스 인사말 문구와 카드, 휴대폰으로 보내는 법](https://sugarmount21.com/apps/sugarcard/christmas-greetings/): 크리스마스 인사말은 받는 사람에 맞춘 한두 문장이면 충분해요. 생생카드에서는 직접 쓴 문구를 크리스마스 카드 29장 중 하나에 얹어 이미지나 눈 내리는 9초 영상으로 보낼 수 있어요.
- [맞춤법 검사기 글자 수 제한, 휴대폰으로 긴 글 검사](https://sugarmount21.com/apps/sugarspeller/long-text-check/): 웹 맞춤법 검사기는 한 번에 300자나 1,000자까지만 받아요. 자기소개서처럼 긴 글은 휴대폰 앱 한글 띄어쓰기로 무료 3,000자, 구독하면 최대 7,000자까지 한 번에 검사할 수 있어요.

## AX notes

How SugarMount apps are built and shipped with an AI coding agent, with measured numbers. Index: https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/ · Korean: https://sugarmount21.com/ax/

### Working with agents

- [gcloud 'This app is blocked' for GA4: impersonate](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/gcloud-blocked-app-impersonation/): Adding YouTube and analytics scopes to a gcloud login hit Google's 'This app is blocked' page three times. Impersonating a service account got a GA4 token.
- [Claude Code login and a first unattended question](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/windows-harness-claude-code-login/): Sign in to Claude Code from Windows PowerShell, ask a first question with claude -p, give scheduled jobs their own sign-in, and see when a sign-in ends.
- [Run a first Claude Code harness job with the kit](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/windows-harness-first-job/): Download the practice harness kit, unzip it, allow scripts in one PowerShell window only, then run the hello job and read the log, report and state file.
- [Open PowerShell and paste your first command](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/windows-harness-powershell-basics/): For readers who have never used a command window: check your Windows version, open the right PowerShell, paste a command and read your user folder path.
- [Capping Vertex AI test costs: a 2,500 KRW stop line missed a 2,956 KRW bill, so we changed the defaults](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/vertex-test-cost-hard-cap/): Our evaluation runner stopped at 2,500 KRW, yet billing showed 2,956 KRW: its ledger counted only responses. Deploys now dry-run and a missing cap means zero.
- [Install Git and Claude Code on Windows](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/windows-harness-claude-code-install/): Download Git for Windows from its official page and install it, then install Claude Code with one PowerShell line and confirm it with claude doctor.
- [Install Docker Desktop on Windows with WSL 2](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/windows-harness-docker-desktop/): Install WSL and Docker Desktop on Windows Pro, Enterprise or Education and test it with hello-world. The part 6 kit runs without Docker, so this is optional.
- [Run Claude Code on a schedule: what a harness is](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/windows-harness-overview/): A harness has Claude Code on one Windows PC write your morning GA4 report, ad budget check and video plan. How it differs from chat AI, and what it needs.
- [Run Claude Code every day with Task Scheduler](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/windows-harness-task-scheduler/): Use the kit's register-job.ps1 to schedule the hello job in Windows Task Scheduler for 09:05 daily, start it once now, and check the result in the status table.
- [When Claude breaks a rule written in CLAUDE.md: six incidents and what came back](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/claude-md-rule-incidents/): Six rules paired with their incidents, two of them recounted from session logs: one rule broke on five later dates, and exit 144 hit 7 more times.
- [GA4 shows zero? Read a table report's total row first](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/ga4-zero-report-reversed/): An AI agent read the GA4 overview's no-data cards as zero for 28 days; a table report's total row had 43 users and 10,522 events. What each zero means.
- [Leaving WSL for native Windows: a checklist for moving a Claude Code dev environment](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/wsl-to-windows-claude-code/): Moving a Claude Code setup from WSL to native Windows: repos took a day, session logs and Docker five. Checked with an R8 release build and 1,500 monkey events.
- [What survives Claude Code auto-compaction: the summary, recent files and the memory index](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/compaction-summary-memory/): A Claude Code session ran 13 days through 9 auto-compactions. No summary kept why the budget was 2,000 won; a stale memory index line likely misled the agent.
- [What survives when a subagent hits its usage limit: raw files on disk, not the report](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/subagent-brief-rules/): When a subagent hits a usage limit, the report it made first is nearly empty. How five cut-off agents were taken over, and a brief that names raw-output paths.
- [Every branch passed its AI review, and the merged code still had 12 defects](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/integration-review-defects/): 13 branches passed agent review and CI; a review of the merged code still confirmed 12 defects. By our count, 10 broke contracts between two packages.
- [Several AI agents in one repository: give every shared file exactly one owner](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/file-owner-table/): A commit swept 50 files from another Claude session into a release fix. We then gave each shared file one owner; git shows why 7 of 13 merges still needed help.
- [Three agent designs, three judges: the market judge alone would have picked the one that crashed on every KakaoTalk file](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/three-designs-three-judges/): Before coding a document viewer, 3 agent designs competed and 3 judges scored them. A crash on every KakaoTalk file and 23 plan gaps surfaced before code.
- [Commits without a Co-Authored-By trailer: the agent made 26 of the 29 we could check](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/co-authored-by-trailer-audit/): We checked 29 commits without a Co-Authored-By trailer against agent session logs: the agent made 26, mostly merges. Commands to count your own repository.
- [A permission table for a scheduled AI agent: what it does alone, and which clicks a person makes](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/agent-permission-table/): Our scheduled AI marketing agent reads one permission table every run. An approved ad restart click was still refused by a tool check, so a person clicked it.
- [How to trust an AI agent's code review: fix only the findings other agents could not refute](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/agent-review-refutation/): SugarSpeller 1.6.025's release review ran 84 agents with three refuters per finding. 20 findings survived, one of them a crash, and the second pass confirmed 0.
- [How many AI coding agents can run at once? Memory and test phones set our limit at three](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/parallel-agent-workstreams/): We were allowed hundreds of AI coding agents, yet only three code-writing agents ever ran at once. 4 GB of free RAM and two shared test phones set that limit.
- [How to write AGENTS.md: only the rules an AI coding agent gets wrong](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/agents-md/): AGENTS.md is the file an AI coding agent reads before it works. Ours has 96 lines, lists only the rules the agent gets wrong, and enforces key ones with tests.

### Testing and release

- [Our release gates were checking something other than the release: a plaintext AAB and one missing dart-define](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/gate-checked-wrong-artifact/): A plaintext-signaling AAB passed one gate; another judged a classpath the intended build never used. How to match gate inputs and keep a must-fail fixture.
- [A malicious file set for a document viewer: ZIP bombs, CFB loops and XSS, generated and wired into tests](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/docviewer-malicious-file-set/): Our Korean document viewer generates 50 hostile files in Python and checks each verdict in unit tests. Which bombs pass the ratio rule, where XSS checks run.
- [Silently skipped tests keep CI green: three crypto cross-checks and an integration test that went stale for six days](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/silent-skip-green-ci/): Our Flutter app's 3 crypto cross-check tests skipped without a Python module that CI never installed, and one of the 13 recorded skips was broken for 6 days.
- [The 95.2% realism score never came out of the runner, and the 3D view was a fixed drawing](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/realism-score-not-3d/): An AI agent's commit claimed 95.2% realism for a 3D trunk simulator. No file holds that number, the runner returned constants, and the view was not 3D.
- [Seven edited HWP files in Hancom's Android apps: 7 of 7 opened, and the re-save waited for a human sign-in](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/hwp-hancom-resave-check/): Seven HWP files edited by SugarDoc, checked in Hancom's two Android apps on a Galaxy S21: all 7 opened cleanly; 2 of 2 re-saved after the operator signed in.
- [A shared LLM cache could have frozen a prompt injection: the blind A/B that let us stop sending context](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/llm-cache-no-context/): A shared LLM cache keyed without the context could serve one injected answer to every user. A blind A/B showed the context added nothing: 96.0% vs 96.6%.
- [Keeping secrets away from an AI coding agent: one rule for chat, logs and token permissions](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/secrets-three-layers/): Three ways secrets leak around an AI coding agent: a key in a session log, two exceptions a copied masking regex missed, a deploy plan asking for a wider token.
- [What "100% E2E pass" really meant: deleting seven runners with zero expect() calls](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/zero-expect-e2e-runners/): Seven runners behind a "100% E2E pass" since Aug 2025 had zero expect() calls; five never called the app. The night we deleted them, a real E2E logged 7 bugs.
- [We built an edit feature and shipped it switched off: the HWP save gate that caught a form-field bug](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/hwp-edit-save-gate/): A gate that diffs edited HWP files record by record caught a form-field bug. 1.1.0 shipped with edit behind a flag; 1.3.0 turned it on nine days later.
- [Our contrast checker passed while skipping 40% of the text: make it print how much it measured](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/contrast-checker-missed-40-percent/): A contrast check that passed in three themes had silently dropped 3,762 of 9,318 text fragments (40%). Now it prints what it measured and fails on a shortfall.
- [3,066 green tests hid a line that breaks opening the database: checking tests by deleting the guard](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/guard-removal-test/): A P2P chat app passed 3,066 tests while one SQLite pragma, traced through plugin source, kept its database from opening. Now we judge tests by deleting guards.
- [The agent said it was tested. The game crashed on the first tutorial tap: a missing VIBRATE permission and the fresh-install monkey test](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/fresh-install-monkey-test/): Our AI agent called a puzzle game crash-free, then it died on the first tutorial tap: a missing VIBRATE permission. adb monkey on clean data hit it at event 15.
- [What to check before shipping an AI-built Android app: the release gate and an R8 crash](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/release-gate/): Our Android app ran fine in debug but crashed at launch in release after R8 removed a constructor. Now every upload passes three pre-release checks.

### Android development

- [No XML file said white, yet the dialog buttons vanished: three places a theme colour leaked](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/android-theme-color-leak/): The app bar colour, colorPrimary, became dialog and sheet button text at 1.02:1 on white. Three leak paths, a test on the shown view, and hue-locked fixes.
- [Quiz reach rose from 2.6% to 17.7%, and 63% of quiz opens came from one morning notification](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/quiz-reach-entry-point-push/): Quiz reach in a Korean spelling app rose from 2.6% to 17.7%, with 63% of opens from a morning local notification. GA4 numbers, limits and our wrong plan.
- [203 unit tests missed a release-only blank result: R8 and Gson field names](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/r8-gson-field-names/): R8 renamed the Gson fields output and etype to a and b, so release results would have come back empty while 203 unit tests passed. The fix and the dex check.
- [We pressed BACK at seven moments before shipping one 'Save as PDF' button](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/pdf-save-back-seven-points/): We pressed BACK at 7 delays during a direct SAF Save as PDF on a release build. Cancel became done at 0.9 to 1.0 s (S20) and 0.75 to 0.9 s (S21); 0 empty files.
- [The first LLM feature in a spell-check app: cost, model evaluation and daily caps for "Why is this wrong?"](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/llm-explain-cost-limits/): A 59-case eval picked a Gemini model at $0.93 per 1,000 calls, a 3,000-call daily cap in the function limits spend, and an AI Studio 402 moved us to Vertex AI.
- [Fitting a JPEG under a file size limit: quality binary search, a predicted long edge, and a final check against the original](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/jpeg-target-size-search/): Fit a JPEG under a byte limit on Android: quality binary search per resolution, a predicted long edge, a 20-encode cap, and why a 107 KB image grew to 150 KB.
- [On Android, HWPX can arrive as application/octet-stream: an 18-row intent matrix and the intent filter that fits it](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/hwpx-octet-stream-intent-filter/): The same .hwpx reached our viewer as a Hancom MIME type from Samsung My Files and as application/octet-stream from Chrome and Files. 18 rows, one manifest.
- [Pre-gzipping Android assets, measured: zero APK savings, and .pack.gz became .pack with a FileNotFoundException](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/android-assets-gz-suffix/): Five pre-gzipped Android asset packs were 18 bytes each larger than the APK's own deflate, and the .gz names vanished, causing FileNotFoundException on launch.
- [A market:// link opens a store chooser on SKT-sold Samsung phones: set the Play package first](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/market-uri-store-chooser/): On two SKT-sold Samsung phones, three store apps answer a market:// link and Android shows a chooser. Setting the Play package first opened Play directly.
- [A splash that never moved on: addOnCompleteListener(this) and onStop](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/splash-listener-onstop/): Our spelling app used addOnCompleteListener(this) for Remote Config; the listener was dropped at onStop, so a screen-off launch never left the splash.
- ["6.7" < "6.11" is false: comparing Remote Config versions as strings froze content updates](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/string-version-compare/): A Korean spelling app compared Remote Config content versions as Kotlin strings, so from 6.10 on, devices stored at 6.2 to 6.9 got no quiz or notice updates.
- [R8 kept 5 AdMob test IDs in our release build: one listOf().any line and a dex count](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/release-ad-id-grep/): A real-ID Block Turn build kept 5 Google test ad strings in its dex. A plain || in place of listOf().any took it to 0. We count IDs and never print them.
- [Android 16 KB page size: add the linker flag before you upgrade the NDK (NDK 27 and 29 tinted our photos blue)](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/ndk-16kb-page-blue-tint/): Six .so files rebuilt for Google Play's 16 KB page rule; NDK 27 and 29 tinted photo transitions blue. Rechecked: NDK 25 aligns to 16 KB with one linker flag.
- [A launch crash only on Android 7: one java.time call in a shared module and a NewApi lint gate](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/android7-java-time-crash/): One java.time call crashed two minSdk 24 games on Android 7. Lint: Call requires API level 26, or core library desugaring. A NewApi gate now blocks release.
- [Android showed some Hangul as blank gaps: NanumSquare's cmap claimed 11,172 syllables but drew only 2,479](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/hangul-blank-glyph-cmap/): An Android app font listed all 11,172 Hangul syllables in its cmap, but 8,693 had no outline, so text vanished with no fallback. Cause, numbers, a check script.
- [androidx.pdf beta01 runs your Application.onCreate a second time, in an isolated process, and the PDF silently never opens](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/androidx-pdf-isolated-process/): androidx.pdf beta01 parses PDFs in an isolated process that also runs your Application.onCreate. Without a guard, the PDF never opened and no error came back.
- [Jetpack Compose splits Korean between syllables, but the stacked 'R/u/l/e' label came from how a Row measures](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/compose-korean-line-break/): Compose can break Korean between syllables, but the label stacked as 'R/u/l/e' on a Galaxy S21 came from Row measurement order. Each cause got its own fix.
- [Play Console said our DEX was 39% optimized. The culprit was a keep rule for an SDK we never used](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/r8-dex-optimization-keep-rule/): Removing -dontoptimize left Play Console's DEX metrics at 36-39%. Deleting an unused Kakao SDK keep rule took r8.json to 85% and the AAB to 11.6 MB.
- [Building an Android HWP viewer: rhwp in a WebView, measured on 222 documents](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/hwp-viewer-rhwp-webview/): The open-source rhwp engine in an Android WebView opened 221 of 222 Korean HWP/HWPX files on a Galaxy S21; a 384-page file needed virtual scrolling.

### Game development

- [We slowed a mini game down twice before checking why it was hard: players couldn't recall the answers](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/spell-rain-difficulty-recall/): We slowed a spelling mini game twice. In a player model, the first slowdown still cost beginners a heart in minute one in 100% of runs: the block was recall.
- [Mobile game feel: frame timing showed our heart penalty landing 109 ms before the collision](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/game-feel-frame-review/): Tapping a blocked arrow changed the heart 109 ms before contact. How the code and recorded frames exposed the order, and what moved to the moment of contact.
- [Rapid taps and an unlocked Retry button: a 600 ms result-card lock, and the 28 crashes a stress run found next](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/result-card-tap-through/): Rapid taps drained every heart within 250 ms, and the next loss card had an unlocked Retry button. A 600 ms lock went in; a stress run later found 28 crashes.
- [A reverse-construction generator and the gate behind 1,100 arrow-puzzle levels](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/arrow-puzzle-level-generator/): All 1,100 Arrow Knots levels come from a reverse-construction generator and pass the G2 pack gate. Fixing the move rule first made each board solvable as built.
- [Testers said the time was "too long, so it's easy": checking that with a simulation before cutting puzzle par times by 30%](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/puzzle-time-limit-simulation/): Testers said our puzzle game gave too much time. A 158-level simulation set the cut at 30%; a 45% cut left casual players a 1% three-star rate past level 500.
- [Puzzle game day-one churn: per-device event timelines, exact board math and four walls in chapter one](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/puzzle-first-chapter-walls/): 7 of 16 ad-acquired devices stalled on board 4 of a block puzzle without a solve. Per-device event timelines and exact per-board win rates found four walls.
- [Block puzzle difficulty: how simulation bots caught a game you could never lose](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/block-puzzle-bot-playtest/): Our block puzzle spec promised every tray could always be placed. A planning bot then played 80 games; all 80 hit the 3,000-move cap. How two bots set the fix.

### Play Store and monetization

- [App campaign ad assets from gameplay recordings](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/game-ad-creatives-from-play-recordings/): Screen recording added to our store-screenshot code produced 24 images and 6 videos for a Google Ads app campaign; a second cut needed only a new JSON spec.
- [GA4 CSV export to a daily morning report](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/windows-harness-ga4-report/): Download a GA4 report as CSV, drop it in a folder, and a scheduled Claude Code job writes a morning report with three key numbers and what you should check.
- [A daily Google Ads budget check that only suggests](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/windows-harness-google-ads/): Export your Google Ads campaign table as CSV and a scheduled Claude Code job suggests budget raises and cuts by fixed rules. You make every change yourself.
- [TikTok, Reels and Shorts plans with Claude Code](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/windows-harness-shorts/): The kit's shorts-plan job reads your game notes and past view counts, then writes today's video plan: shot list, captions and posting times. You film and post.
- [17 days of a Claude Code harness: how to start](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/windows-harness-game-marketing/): From 17 days of a game-marketing harness: 7 failed cells out of 51, an "ok" that hid zero posts, a sign-in expiry warning, and which job to switch on first.
- [GMA Next-Gen called our full-screen ad callback on a background thread: how a photo app crashed after 243 passing unit tests](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/gma-next-gen-callback-thread/): Interstitial code that passed 243 unit tests crashed on the emulator: GMA Next-Gen calls ad callbacks off the main thread, and UMP starts each launch at false.
- [Four Google Ads app campaigns, $36.4, 105 installs, about 3% ROAS: CPI ran 30 times break-even](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/google-ads-break-even-cpi/): Four Google Ads app campaigns for two puzzle games spent $36.4 for 105 installs. The best, Block Turn KR, made about 3% ROAS at 30 times its break-even CPI.
- [We set interstitial frequency from device timelines, and tutorials don't count](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/interstitial-frequency-timeline/): Our block puzzle's first interstitial came 91 s into a fresh install, before any real puzzle. Now tutorials don't count and a classic game over counts twice.
- [A month of 'temporary error': our subscription details screen never waited for products, and 1 of 16 users started checkout](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/subscription-details-94-percent/): A Play review said the premium plan showed a 'temporary error' for a month. The details screen never waited for products: 1 of 16 users reached checkout.
- [GA4 said 19 installs yesterday and 8 were real: filtering out test phones and Play pre-launch and review devices](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/ga4-test-device-filter/): sdk_gphone64_arm64 and sdk_gphone16k_arm64 in GA4 were Play pre-launch and review devices. How we filter them and our own test phones out of install counts.
- [A 20% staged rollout went out at 100%: a completed release in the Play Publisher API cannot go back to staged](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/play-staged-rollout-completed/): SugarSpeller 1.6.029 was meant for 20% via the Play Publisher API but was committed as completed; Play refused the move back to 20% with a 403. Cause and guard.

### Website and search

- [App privacy policy templates: we threw ours out and rewrote it from a code audit](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/privacy-policy-code-audit/): Four Android apps shared a generated policy saying nothing was collected, yet one sent requests to our server. How a source audit rewrote 8 pages, with steps.
- [4.5:1 contrast in the site build: the dark hover pair that failed for 7 of 11 apps](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/build-measures-contrast/): Our site build computes 143 contrast pairs from 13 app accents and fails below 4.5:1. A dark hover pair failed for 7 of 11 apps; a CSS swap still slips past.
- [Search Console showed 'Couldn't fetch' for ten days; a new domain property processed the same sitemaps in seconds](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/gsc-sitemap-couldnt-fetch/): Search Console showed the sitemap as 'Couldn't fetch' for ten days, yet the API said isPending=True and Googlebot fetched it. A domain property took seconds.
- [Structured data after FAQ rich results ended: what we kept for GEO](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/structured-data-after-faq-rich-results/): Google ended FAQ rich results on May 7, 2026 and Naver on July 9. Why our 106 FAQPage pages stay untouched, and the feed, date and app markup we fixed instead.
- [Keeping a static site safe when several AI agents edit it: one --check before every commit](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/static-site-check-gate/): Several AI agent sessions edit this GitHub Pages site; one --check before each commit demands zero rebuild changes and zero gate errors. Four times it stopped.
- [Privacy policy AI processing location (cross-border transfer): a notice fixed twice in one day, then tied to code](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/ai-region-privacy-policy/): A Vertex AI global endpoint cannot be named as one country, so our privacy policy says processing may happen outside Korea, tied to code and CI.
- [Every sitemap lastmod had the same date: deriving modified dates from a content hash](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/sitemap-lastmod-content-hash/): All 51 sitemap URLs once shared one lastmod. Now dates follow a hash of each page's main content, not commit dates, and a 99-file commit moved only 6 of them.

### Retrospectives and numbers

- [Flutter vs native solo dev: one studio, two picks](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/flutter-vs-native-solo-dev/): One solo studio picked Kotlin native for its utility apps and Flutter for a family app, 15 days apart. What split them, a flawed AI estimate, a 2-week spike.
- [10,001 lines of greeting cards: built with an AI agent, removed with one](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/greeting-card-removal/): We deleted 10,001 lines of AI-built greeting cards. With R8 in the same release, the APK fell from 25.66 to 13.15 MB; about 11 MB was card assets.
- [Daily users rose after the redesign while organic D1 retention fell from 15.2% to 11.2%](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/retention-cohort-break/): After an August 2025 redesign, D1 retention of our spelling app's organic cohorts fell from 15.2% to 11.2%; 70% of lost daily users were 31-365 days old.
- [We built three photo apps before checking the market: this year's new apps had a median of 1,166 installs](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/market-check-before-app/): We scraped Google Play only after building three photo apps. The 32 compress apps from 2026 had a median of 1,166 installs; 11 apps were logged as on hold.
- [A year of AI coding in 701 commits: from "complete" to cause and verification](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/commit-messages-701/): 701 commits recounted: after adopting AI, messages grew from 26 to 233 characters, but fixes stating a cause went from 1 of 29 to 56 of 73 only a year later.
- [How we shipped four Android apps in 20 days with an AI coding agent](https://sugarmount21.com/en/ax/20-days-4-apps/): A solo developer and Claude Code put four Android apps on Google Play within 20 days of the first commit. 52 of 59 commits were co-authored with the agent.
